newsitem.title: USA: American General, USLife to merge - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: American General, USLife to merge - WSJ.

text.p: American General Corp is expected to announce today a pact to pay as much as $1.8 billion for USLife Corp, the Wall Street Journal said Thursday.
American General also will assume as much as $600 million of USLife's debt, the paper reported, citing people familiar with the matter.
The USLife deal, for between $47 and $49 a share in stock, is designed to boost earnings growth and gain economies of scale for American General, the paper said.
USLife shares closed Wednesday at 41-3/4. American General closed up 7/8 at 41-1/2.
Speculation arose that USLife would be a takeover target as the term of its 76-year-old chairman, Gordon Crosby, neared an end and Crosby remained silent over any decision to seek another term.

Thursday's report said the two companies were helped in reaching a pact by the long relationship between Crosby and American General Chairman Harold Hook, who was a top executive at USLife before leaving in 1970.
